preconditions.description: The number of elements in the array is between 2 and 100,000.
The number of elements that can be changed is between 0 and the minimum of 10 and N-2.
Each element in the array is between -10^9 and 10^9.

postconditions.description: The output array has the same number of elements as the input array.

postconditions.expression: all(isinstance(x, int) for x in return_value)
postconditions.description: All elements in the output array are integers.

postconditions.expression: sum(1 for i in range(N-1) if return_value[i+1] != return_value[i] + d) <= K
postconditions.description: The number of changes made to form an arithmetic progression is at most K.

postconditions.expression: all(return_value[i+1] == return_value[i] + d for i in range(N-1))
postconditions.description: The output array forms an arithmetic progression with a constant difference d.

postconditions.expression: all((return_value[0] < other[0]) or (return_value[0] == other[0] and return_value[1] < other[1]) for other in all_possible_progressions)
postconditions.description: Among all possible arithmetic progressions, the output is the most beautiful one.
